items.text: There is a doc comment sitting directly above the function at all — a function with no doc block is a fail before anything else is read.
The doc says what the function does; a comment that only restates the function's own name teaches the reader nothing and is a fail.
The doc names every parameter in the signature with its meaning — and never names a parameter the signature does not have, because that is simply wrong.
The doc states what the function returns, so the reader learns the contract without reading the body.

liveNotes: The confirmed plan asked for two things a command can decide — the JSDoc contract over src/, and that `npm test` still passes — so the close is: guards, then typecheck + test work stages, then ONE judged-floor stage last for the three doc-comment facts (has-doc, params, returns) plus the prose quality (says-what) that no command can render.

The person asked for things that NOTHING in this close checks, and no stage claims them: (a) 'Do not change any function behaviour or signature' — a test suite that still passes cannot show that no signature or behaviour changed; (b) that the doc prose genuinely teaches the contract rather than restating the name — the judged floor's says-what line asks for it, but the arbiter's rulebook may render it over quotes only, so this is judgement, not measurement.

The judged-floor stage names 8 artifacts because the kind caps paths at 8; src/ has 11 modules, so src/email.js, src/sink.js and src/dumpers.js are NOT judged by it. Nothing in the facts object says which of the 11 modules export functions, so the 8 chosen are the entry module (src/index.js, which package.json points `types` at) plus the modules the test files are named after (digest, backup, deliver, fallback) plus the core pipeline/collection modules (run, checks, metrics). The three left out are a known blind spot, not a claim that they need no docs.

Whether prose 'says what the function does' is inherently judgement; the mechanical JSDoc-related stages a genre could use (tsc's checkJs anti-drift gate) check ONLY that existing @param/@returns tags agree with the code — they cannot count doc blocks that do not exist. That is why every doc-comment item lives in the judged-floor stage and no count-not-worse stage pretends to measure them.
No lint instrument exists to name: the facts object records that the repo deliberately has no ESLint/Prettier config and CI states no lint step, so no lint stage was composed.

typecheck-errors-in-src is a no-regression floor of 0 (the repo is tsc-clean at seed); it grades the risk that adding @param/@returns tags changes what checkJs infers and introduces a type error. typecheck-errors-outside-src is the ceiling over everything outside src/ with its baseline measured from this run's own seed, which the genre requires whenever a typecheck stage is scoped to a subset of the tree.

The test stages read Node's TAP summary lines, which name no file path; the scope prefix (test/) therefore cannot exclude any of them and the summary lines are kept whole-suite. The executed count (^# tests) is the honest denominator rather than the passed count, and suite-green is split into two assertions: the runner must exit 0 AND report zero failing tests.

I could not read the repository, so I could not verify which src modules actually contain exported functions, nor whether src/index.js is a re-export barrel; the judged-floor card's has-doc line is left to the arbiter's rulebook to apply per artifact.
